output.summary: A parasitic perennial flowering plant of dry, often saline habitats. It lacks chlorophyll and lives mostly underground attached to a host’s roots, producing a fleshy, club-shaped mass of minute dark-red or purplish flowers after winter rain.
output.edibilityNote: Bedouin people ate cleaned, peeled fresh spikes; it was also a famine food, last reported in the 19th-century Canary Islands.
